basis: Complement immunodeficiency; infections are secondary diseases, and associated lupus occurs in only 10-20%.
Primary glial neoplasm of the central nervous system.
Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid-cell malignancy; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune axis.
Melanoma arising in the iris.
Umbrella for abnormal metabolic processes; no additional organ is consistently affected across the group.
Myofibrillar muscle degeneration defines disease; global developmental delay in 1/2 annotated patients supports neurologic involvement. Dysphagia can reflect muscle weakness.
Mesomelic skeletal dysplasia with synostoses and joint restriction; ocular and intellectual abnormalities occur in <30%; dimples do not indicate skin damage.
Leukocyte dysfunction defines immunodeficiency; lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia is annotated at 30-79%. Recurrent infections are secondary diseases.
Isolated inherited cataract affecting the lens.
Joint/connective-tissue abnormalities and skin fragility or hyperextensibility define EDS; vascular damage is not common across unspecified dominant forms.
Structural narrowing of the lower oesophagus.
Treponemal infection directly inflames the brain.
Carcinoma arising in the gallbladder or extrahepatic biliary tract; adjacent-organ invasion is variable and stage-dependent.
Calculus of a salivary gland or its duct; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Trochlear nerve dysfunction; impaired eye movement reflects nerve palsy rather than direct damage to the eye.
Microcephaly and intellectual disability define neurodevelopmental disease; macrotia alone does not establish ear dysfunction.
Immature germ-cell tumour of the CNS pineal region; endocrine dysfunction is not a defining feature.
Benign adipose tumour occupying the external ear.
Neoplasm of the orbital compartment; bone involvement is not shared by most orbital neoplasms.
Purine salvage disorder; nephropathy and intellectual disability/dystonia each annotated at 30-79%. Neurologic severity varies; gout and stones are separate diseases.
Dermal histiocytic neoplasm, a non-Langerhans histiocytosis; ocular and other systemic involvement occur in <30%.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis in this scheme.
Raised fascial-compartment pressure compromises skeletal muscle; lasting nerve injury depends on severity and duration, without established ≥30% frequency.
Palmoplantar keratoderma and sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; both occur in 80-99%.
Isolated unilateral shortening of toe bones.
